text:
maya (Eng Manager): Heads up 0% asking: planning to promote Kai from L4 -> L5 (IC) effective 2026-08-01. Kai is based in Berlin and we'd like to do a market adjustment + equity refresh. What are the cross-border considerations and approvals for non-US employees?

leo (People Ops): Congrats to Kai! Cross-border has a few extra steps: local labor law check, payroll tax handling, and local benefits alignment. For EU employees we need HRBP + local payroll team sign-off and ensure the effective date meets local contract amendment notice periods.

anna (Compensation): For comp approvals: base increase within band & <=10% = manager + director approval. Anything >10% or above band midpoint requires comp committee. Equity refreshes follow the Equity Grant Request flow; for EMEA employees we also need stock plan admin sign-off for local docs.

maya (Eng Manager): Good to know. We were thinking +11% base and a small one-time RSU refresh. So sounds like comp committee will be needed. Any special packet items for international cases?

felix (Finance): From finance: include payroll currency and GL mapping for DE entity. If approving mid-cycle you must specify effective date and whether payroll should gross up for employer-side tax (if applicable). Retro pay for non-US payrolls often takes 1-2 pay runs to process; include backpay calc if requesting.

payroll-bot: FYI: Berlin payroll cutoff for August effective changes is 2026-07-15 12:00 CEST. Approvals after cutoff will apply to September payroll. See https://intra.redwood/payroll/eu.

tax-bot: Reminder: RSU/refresh grants may trigger different tax-withholding rules in DE; comp team must coordinate with Stock Plan Admin. Tax advice is not legal advice; consult external counsel for edge cases.

maya (Eng Manager): If committee is needed, how long is the queue? We have a product milestone and want the effective date to align with it.

anna (Compensation): Committee meets Tuesdays. Typical turnaround is 3-5 business days if packet is complete. For international promotions include translated job summary + local market comp data (benchmarks in EUR). Mark "expedite" with business case if you need faster review.

kai (IC): Quick question as the impacted person: will my benefits change (pension, health) or my bonus target prorate? Also curious about equity vesting implications for the refresh.

suzie (HRBP): Good Q. Local benefits that are tied to level may change; HRBP will update pension contributions & benefits eligibility effective the promotion date. Bonus target will be prorated from the effective date if target changes. New equity refresh vests per the grant terms and is independent of prior awards.

maya (Eng Manager): What's the minimal set to submit so the committee doesn't bounce it for missing docs?

leo (People Ops): Minimal packet for comp committee: 1) Manager justification (1-paragraph + 3 bullets of impact), 2) Updated scorecard, 3) Proposed comp table (current vs proposed, currency), 4) Equity ask & draft grant type, 5) Local payroll & GL code, 6) Any peer benchmark data. For EMEA add HRBP note about contract amendment notice.

anna (Compensation): + include a short headcount cost projection for the remainder of the quarter and next fiscal year. If >12% change or >$15k run-rate delta, VP Finance approval needed.

maya (Eng Manager): Any wording examples for the manager justification? Trying to keep it concise.

leo (People Ops): Example: "Recommend promoting Kai to L5 effective 2026-08-01 for increased scope: ownership of Model Serving infra (reduced latency 30%), led cross-region rollout, and mentored 3 ICs. Requesting +11% base (EUR) and one-time RSU refresh to align to local market median.)"

maya (Eng Manager): Perfect. One more: can we backdate the effective date to include the sprint that shipped in June? Kai started the extra scope back then.

felix (Finance): Backdating is possible but limited. We generally allow retro effective dates up to 60 days prior to submission for EU payrolls. Backpay calculations must be attached. Anything older requires VP approval + legal review.

payroll-bot: Reminder: Retro pay requests for EU must be submitted with payroll supporting doc and approved before 2026-07-10 COB to run in August payroll. See https://intra.redwood/payroll/backpay-eu.

anna (Compensation): If you plan to include retroactive equity or change vesting schedules, that complicates things. Best to set grant date = submission date unless within 30 days of the desired effective date and Stock Plan Admin approves.

maya (Eng Manager): Thanks. Last item: salary compression concerns. Kai's bump will be near peer median, but one of our L5s in US is at higher USD equivalent. Any guidance on cross-currency fairness?

leo (People Ops): We don't equalize absolute USD across regions. We benchmark per-market. However comp committee considers internal parity within the local org. Provide peer comps in EUR for DE peers; note differences with US peers but committee typically keeps market-adjusted expectations.

anna (Compensation): If compression is an internal issue within the same legal entity, comp team will flag remedies (market adjustments, merit increases) during calibration. For cross-entity differences, document the market rationale.

maya (Eng Manager): Great. I'll prepare the packet with the manager justification, updated scorecard, local benchmarks, GL code, and backpay calc (requesting 30 days retro). I'll tag @anna and @suzie for pre-check before submission.

kai (IC): Thanks everyone 1 appreciate the clarity. Happy to help with evidence/examples for the packet. :smile:
